summary: Phase 23 stop-the-line record for a possible severity increase on a registered capital finding (23-SPEC line 103). While registering AUD-ANTIRUG-024 the 23-01 executor re-read the related HTTP poller finding AUD-ANTIRUG-018 (S2, STRAND, confirmed) and found its rationale ("only chains running without a WebSocket URL, after an outage larger than the provider range limit ... Protection then stays off until restart") wrong on two points, confirmed by the execute-phase orchestrator re-reading the code at HEAD. (1) A restart does not clear it: the HTTP poller re-reads its start block from chain_state on restart (src/anti-rug/detector.ts:1228-1232 at the audit base, :1231-1235 at HEAD); the row advances only after a successful poll (:1300-1306 base, :1303-1309 HEAD) or a tick with no registered positions (:1269-1276 base, :1272-1279 HEAD); held positions are re-registered before the poller starts (src/bot.ts:2120-2144 base, :2122-2146 HEAD). (2) Ordinary downtime triggers it: getLogs requests lastBlock+1..currentBlock in one call (:1279-1291 base, :1282-1294 HEAD) and the repo's own range assumption is 10 blocks on ETH ("Alchemy free-tier safe", src/chainRegistry.ts:223-230) and 500 elsewhere, so about two minutes of downtime on ETH is enough. It is silent: the dashboard shows the chain connected (AUD-ANTIRUG-007) and only antirug.http-polling.error log lines appear. Not reproduced; whether the operator's provider refuses these ranges is unmeasured. The operator was asked what grade it should have and whether any chain runs without a WebSocket URL.
